A Texas school district has invested $11 million to fully adopt iPads and MacBook Neo devices. The Beaumont Independent School District has decided to phase out its fleet of Chromebooks in favor of Apple products, with officials stating that the new equipment outperforms in reliability, cost, and efficiency.

According to a report this week by the Beaumont Enterprise, the Beaumont Independent School District Board of Trustees has approved a four-year lease agreement worth $11.19 million to upgrade the district's technology equipment system.

As part of the deal, the district will provide a total of 14,585 Apple devices to teachers and students from pre-kindergarten through high school. The new batch of Apple devices will replace a fleet of Chromebooks that have been in use for many years, many of which were purchased over five years ago. The district spends nearly $500,000 annually on maintenance and support for its Chromebook fleet.

The new plan includes providing over 4,000 iPads for pre-kindergarten through second-grade students, and 9,500 MacBook Neo devices for students from third grade through 12th grade; the district has also set aside 1,000 MacBook Neo devices for teachers.

The district compared the MacBook Neo with products from Lenovo and Asus, ultimately concluding that the MacBook Neo had "the strongest performance and stability among the tested devices." Apple's more favorable financing terms, along with access to AppleCare services, were also significant factors in the decision.
